item.brief: Operator request (authenticated): our books now hold more than one currency. Change the reports program (Python) that reads the ledger CSV on stdin and prints per-account totals, per the shared contract. Totals must be per account and currency, output header account,currency,total_cents, rows sorted by account then currency. Input without a currency column (old ledger output) counts as USD. A malformed currency code prints an error to stderr and exits with status 2. Add unittest coverage, keep python3 -m unittest passing, update README, and commit locally. Do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

Input without a currency column counts as USD. Assumption: the header change is an intended breaking change per the shared contract.
pr.summary: made reports totals per account and currency. now can read multi-currency ledgers and rejects malformed currency codes. before: account,total_cents with all currencies summed together; now: account,currency,total_cents, sorted by account then currency, legacy input counted as USD, malformed currency exits 2.

risk.why: CLI output header and column layout change (account,total_cents becomes account,currency,total_cents), which breaks any caller parsing the output. Behaviour change in reports.py plus tests and README. Reviewer confirmed high.

item.brief: Operator request (authenticated): our books now hold more than one currency. Change the ledger (Rust) program that converts a TSV of transactions on stdin into CSV on stdout, per the shared contract. Add the optional fourth currency column with validation (exactly three uppercase ASCII letters; default USD), output the currency column in the header and on every row, and make a malformed currency print an error naming the line number to stderr and exit with status 2 (other input errors keep exit 1). Add tests for the new behaviour, keep cargo test passing, update README, and commit locally. Do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

state.summary:
Ledger now takes an optional fourth TSV currency column (exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, default USD) and emits `date,account,amount_cents,currency` with a currency on every row. A malformed currency prints `line N: bad currency ...` to stderr and exits 2; other input errors still exit 1. Committed locally as 1b7c3ed on archon/mpc0ktrv-operator-request-authenticated-our-books; not pushed. Checks on the final head (tree 6cac9477262f8477c04c2b854aa9eaeaa2601df6): `cargo test` passes (3 CLI tests, 7 library tests, 0 failures) and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. Before this change, `cargo fmt --check` already failed on the untouched tree, so I did not reformat. Rust was not installed, so I installed it with rustup (stable, minimal profile plus clippy and rustfmt). The ledger has no Python code, so `python3 -m unittest` does not apply here. The reports side is the sibling item qi_01M7W30S65847EFVPKP56N20Z7 and was not touched. Review: reviewer agt_01M7W34D55HMPT8YVTFFPQ3A35 passed the head with no blocking findings. Open non-blocking follow-ups: a trailing tab now exits 2 with `bad currency ""` where it used to exit 1, which the README does not document; currency is whitespace-trimmed, so ' EUR' is accepted; the public lib API changed (parse_line returns ParseError, Entry has a new pub currency field), which breaks downstream struct literals and may need a version bump; no test covers CRLF or a trailing tab. Nothing is left running. The cargo target is in the item cache, which Archon deletes when the item ends.

pr.body: Approach: parse_line returns ParseError, an enum with Input (exit 1) and Currency (exit 2) variants. The binary maps the variant to its exit status. Entry gains a currency field and to_csv_row emits it. Files: src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/ledger.rs, tests/cli.rs (new), README.md. Checks: cargo test passes (3 CLI, 7 library); clippy clean with -D warnings. cargo fmt --check already failed on the base tree, so it was not reformatted. Assumptions: currency is trimmed like the other fields; a missing column means USD. Known limits: a trailing tab now exits 2 (previously 1); lib API is breaking for parse_line's error type and Entry literals.
pr.summary: ledger accepts an optional 4th currency column (3 uppercase letters, default USD) and exports a currency column. before: 3-column CSV, no currency. now: 4-column CSV; bad currency exits 2, other errors exit 1.
pr.title: Add currency column to ledger export

risk.why: CLI output format change (new currency column) consumed by the reports tool, and a public lib API change (ParseError, Entry.currency). Behaviour changed; tests added and run. Reviewer confirmed high.
